Graphite (natural): Mozambique → United States (concentrate, sea) · Flake graphite concentrate shipped from Balama to Syrah's Vidalia AAM plant in Louisiana. Balama sold 55 kt to ex-China destinations in 2025 (all destinations combined, not US-only); Vidalia's throughput requirement at 11,250 t/yr AAM nameplate is a fraction of that. No US-specific tonnage published.

Graphite (natural): Madagascar → Germany (concentrate, sea) · Coarse 'SuperFlake' concentrate (94-97% C) exported via Port of Tulear; first full container loads delivered to Germany and the USA in Oct-Nov 2024 under existing offtakes, serving consumer electronics and fire-retardant applications. Tonnage not disclosed; mine total run-rate is only ~11 kt/yr. Germany's BGR assessed Madagascar as a strategic graphite supplier for the EU battery industry (2026).

Graphite (natural): China → South Korea (component, sea) · Spherical graphite and anode active material; no tonnage established. Context: Benchmark put Chinese production at 74% of the whole graphite anode supply chain, with <1% of uncoated spherical graphite made outside China (2023). From late 2023 Beijing required export permits for high-purity, high-hardness and large-flake natural graphite and for spherical graphite, making Korean anode makers' access conditional rather than embargoed.

Graphite (natural): China → United States (component, sea) · Anode-grade graphite/AAM, under active trade restriction; no tonnage established. July 2025: US Commerce set a 93.5% preliminary anti-dumping duty on Chinese anode-grade graphite (final AD/CVD due Q1 2026). US tariff on Chinese natural graphite rises 0% to 25% from 2026, and the Treasury exemption allowing Chinese graphite in EV-tax-credit-eligible batteries runs only to 2027. US AAM imports from ex-China sources reportedly grew ~5x y/y in 2025-26.

Nickel: Indonesia → China (concentrate, sea) · MHP intermediate. NATIONAL: Indonesian MHP output +64% y/y to 360,000 t gross product Jan-Sep 2025, mostly to Chinese sulphate/precursor plants; MHP ~35-40% Ni, 2-4% Co. ROUTE SHOWN: intra-group HNC (60 kt/yr Ni-eq) to Huayou Quzhou, which feeds on MHP, matte and Ni powder. Group MHP shipments 236,500 t in 2025 (+30%); split by receiving plant NOT disclosed. 2026 RISK: export delays from Indonesian REE/radioactivity screening.

Nickel: New Caledonia → South Korea (raw, sea) · Saprolite ore from SMSP's NMC mines in New Caledonia to the SNNC RKEF smelter at Gwangyang. Mines started at 1.8 Mt/yr ore capacity and have increased to ~3.4 Mt/yr at ~2% Ni grade (JV partner disclosure). Feeds ~54 kt/yr Ni in ferronickel, shifting partly to matte for battery use.

Nickel: South Korea → South Korea (concentrate, road) · Domestic matte leg on the same industrial complex: under a 2023 agreement SNNC builds a matte unit to supply POSCO's nickel sulphate/high-purity nickel plant, eventually ~21,000 t/yr matte (~75% Ni) upgraded to >99.9% nickel, nameplate 20,000 t/yr. Ramp status as of 2026 NOT verified.
